title: Bioelectrically induced two-headed planaria stay two-headed across later regenerations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Bioelectrically induced two-headed planaria stay two-headed across later regenerations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In planarian flatworms the number of heads a regenerating fragment builds is set by the state of a bioelectric circuit with a default of one; transiently modifying it re-sets it to 'two', and the resulting two-headed worms keep regenerating as two-headed through multiple rounds of cutting without further manipulation, unless the pattern is experimentally reset.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Re-writing morphogenetic memories: ontogenetic and evolutionary timescales

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Remarkably, when cut again in multiple subsequent rounds of regeneration (with no further manipulation), the fragments continue to result in two-headed animals. This shift in the target morphology for regeneration is permanent (unless the animal’s bioelectric pattern memory is reset back to a one-headed state by an experimental manipulation).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Re-writing morphogenetic memories: ontogenetic and evolutionary timescales”. Scope: Planarian flatworms (Dugesia japonica), author's lab (Oviedo et al. 2010; Durant et al. 2019)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The repeated-regeneration phenotype is exceptionally direct and feasible to reanalyze if animal-level records are public. The causal assignment to a bioelectric circuit and the unbounded term 'permanent' are less completely resolved.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track treated founders and all fragments through multiple untreated cuts, recording head number and bioelectric state, with sham-treated and reset-to-one controls. Stable two-headed regeneration across lineages, reversed by a targeted bioelectric reset, confirms persistent physiological inheritance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Permanent is bounded by the number of observed rounds.

Raw lineage data may not be deposited.

Persistent drug, microbiome, or epigenetic effects are alternative carriers.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Persistence across amputations and experimental reset are a direct test of a modifiable regenerative target, and the published planarian studies report both. The animal-level lineages are not an open dataset, so the test is a reassessment of those reports. Other stable physiological stores remain live alternatives on the existing evidence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After a transient bioelectric or gap-junction treatment, cut fragments in later rounds with no further drug and record head number, plus a reset cohort returned to one head by a second manipulation. Two-headed regenerates across rounds, reversed by the reset and not by washout alone, would support a stored target; return to one head as soon as the drug is gone, or a heritable mutation, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Round-by-round head counts are in the experimental papers, not a deposited lineage table.

A persistent non-genetic store other than the bioelectric circuit, including bacteria, can keep the two-headed outcome.
